speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have been experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain. To help me determine the cause, can you tell me if your chest pain feels like pressure, squeezing, or burning, and does it radiate to your jaw, neck, or left arm? Also, when did these symptoms first start?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallory-Weiss Syndrome with possible progression to Boerhaave syndrome (esophageal rupture). REQUEST IMAGES: Esophagram or CT Chest to evaluate for esophageal perforation.
